docs.title: Verifying Demo Uploads
docs.text:
This guide explains how to verify that demo uploads are working correctly in the MatchZy Auto Tournament system.

Setup Required

Before verifying demo uploads, make sure you've completed the Demo Upload Setup Guide.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: MatchZy automatically uploads demo files after matches complete. The system receives these uploads via the /api/demos/:matchSlug/upload endpoint and stores them in data/demos/{matchSlug}/.

docs.title: 1. Check Demo Upload Configuration
docs.text:
Before a match starts, verify that demo upload is configured:

API Endpoint: GET /api/demos/:matchSlug/status

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  http://localhost:3000/api/demos/r1m1/status

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "matchSlug": "r1m1",
  "matchId": 1,
  "serverId": "server-123",
  "matchStatus": "loaded",
  "demoUploadConfigured": true,
  "expectedUploadUrl": "https://your-domain.com/api/demos/r1m1/upload",
  "hasDemoFile": false,
  "demoFilePath": null,
  "note": "MatchZy should upload demos to the expected URL after match/map completion"
}

What to check:

  • ✅ demoUploadConfigured should be true
  • ✅ expectedUploadUrl should be a valid URL
  • ⚠️ If demoUploadConfigured is false, check that webhook_url is set in settings

docs.title: 2. Verify Demo Upload Command Was Sent
docs.text:
When a match is loaded, check the logs for:

✓ Demo upload configured for match r1m1 on server-123

Or check the match load response:

API Endpoint: POST /api/matches/:slug/load

The response includes:

{
  "success": true,
  "demoUploadConfigured": true,
  "rconResponses": [
    {
      "success": true,
      "command": "matchzy_demo_upload_url \"https://your-domain.com/api/demos/r1m1/upload\""
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 3. Monitor Demo Upload Logs
docs.text:
Watch the application logs during and after a match. You should see:

When upload starts:

[Demo Upload] Upload request received
  matchSlug: r1m1
  filename: match_demo.dem
  matchId: 12345
  mapNumber: 1

When upload completes:

[Demo Upload] Demo uploaded successfully
  matchSlug: r1m1
  filename: match_demo.dem
  fileSize: 15.23 MB
  path: r1m1/match_demo.dem

docs.title: 4. Check Demo File Exists
docs.text:
After a match completes, verify the demo file was saved:

API Endpoint: GET /api/demos/:matchSlug/info

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  http://localhost:3000/api/demos/r1m1/info

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "hasDemo": true,
  "filename": "match_demo.dem",
  "size": 15972352,
  "sizeFormatted": "15.23 MB"
}

Or check the file system:

ls -lh data/demos/r1m1/
# Should show .dem files

docs.title: 5. Download Demo File
docs.text:
Test downloading the demo:

API Endpoint: GET /api/demos/:matchSlug/download

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN" \
  -o demo.dem \
  http://localhost:3000/api/demos/r1m1/download

docs.title: Demo Upload Not Configured
docs.text:
Symptoms:

  • demoUploadConfigured: false in status endpoint
  • No demo upload command in logs

Solutions:

  1. Ensure webhook_url is set in Settings
  2. Verify SERVER_TOKEN environment variable is set
  3. Check that the match was loaded after webhook URL was configured

docs.title: Demo Upload Fails
docs.text:
Symptoms:

  • Logs show "Failed to configure demo upload"
  • MatchZy server logs show errors

Solutions:

  1. Verify RCON connection to server is working
  2. Check MatchZy plugin version (0.8.24+)
  3. Ensure server can reach the webhook URL (not localhost)
  4. Check server logs for MatchZy errors

docs.title: Demo File Not Received
docs.text:
Symptoms:

  • Match completes but no demo file
  • Status shows hasDemoFile: false

Solutions:

  1. Check MatchZy server logs for upload errors
  2. Verify the upload URL is accessible from the server
  3. Check that SERVER_TOKEN matches in both systems
  4. Verify MatchZy has permission to write demos
  5. Check application logs for upload errors

docs.title: Demo Upload Received But File Missing
docs.text:
Symptoms:

  • Logs show "Demo uploaded successfully"
  • But file doesn't exist on disk

Solutions:

  1. Check disk space: df -h
  2. Verify write permissions on data/demos/ directory
  3. Check application logs for file write errors
  4. Verify the file path is correct

docs.title: Testing Demo Upload Manually
docs.text:
You can test the demo upload endpoint manually using curl:

# Create a dummy demo file
echo "dummy demo content" > test.dem

# Upload it (requires SERVER_TOKEN)
curl -X POST \
  -H "X-MatchZy-Token: YOUR_SERVER_TOKEN" \
  -H "MatchZy-FileName: test_demo.dem" \
  -H "MatchZy-MatchId: 12345" \
  -H "MatchZy-MapNumber: 1" \
  --data-binary @test.dem \
  http://localhost:3000/api/demos/r1m1/upload

Expected Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Demo uploaded successfully",
  "filename": "test_demo.dem"
}

docs.title: Log Locations
docs.text:
• Application logs: Check console output or log files
  • MatchZy server logs: Check CS2 server console/logs
  • Demo files: data/demos/{matchSlug}/

docs.title: Related Endpoints
docs.text:
• GET /api/demos/:matchSlug/status - Check demo upload configuration
  • GET /api/demos/:matchSlug/info - Check if demo file exists
  • GET /api/demos/:matchSlug/download - Download demo file
  • POST /api/demos/:matchSlug/upload - Upload endpoint (used by MatchZy)

docs.title: What to do when something breaks
What to do when something breaks
docs.text: This guide gives you a calm checklist for common problems during a tournament in MatchZy Auto Tournament . For deeper debugging steps, see Troubleshooting.

docs.title: 1. A player cannot connect
docs.text:
Symptoms: Player gets “Auth rejected” or cannot join the server.

Do this:

  1. Pause the match from the match details view.
  2. Confirm the player is on the correct team roster on the Teams page.
  3. If you need a substitute, use Add Backup Player in the match admin controls.
  4. Ask the player to reconnect.

If it still fails, your technical contact can check CS2 server logs and the MatchZy plugin.

docs.title: 2. The server is laggy or unplayable
docs.text:
Symptoms: Everyone reports lag, stutters, or high ping.

Do this:

  1. Pause the match and tell teams you are investigating.
  2. Check the Servers page to see if the server looks healthy.
  3. If you have another server available, consider moving the match there.
  4. Resume the match when both teams agree to continue.

For advanced recovery options (restoring from backups, replaying rounds), see Match Recovery.

docs.title: 3. The match is stuck (warmup, veto, or no progress)
docs.text:
Symptoms: Warmup never ends, veto does not progress, or the match seems frozen.

Do this:

  1. Open the Matches page and click the affected match.
  2. Use admin controls such as:
  3. End Warmup – if players are ready but the game is stuck.
  4. Skip Veto – if veto is blocked and you are okay forcing a map.
  5. Restart Round / Restart Match – as a last resort.
  6. Inform teams clearly what you are doing before pressing these buttons.

If this happens often, your developer can review logs and server configuration.

docs.title: 4. Nothing is updating in the UI
docs.text:
Symptoms: Scores, brackets, or match status do not change even though games are played.

Do this:

  1. Go to Settings and check that the Webhook URL is set to your live domain (for example https://example.com).
  2. Confirm that your CS2 servers are using that same URL for webhooks and demo uploads.
  3. Check the Servers page to ensure servers show as online.

If updates still do not appear, contact your technical contact or open an issue/Discord ticket with logs and screenshots.
